statement: For 0 <= a <= b <= n define sum(a,b) = nums[a] + nums[a+1] + ... + nums[b-1] (the empty sum is 0 when a=b). Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the maximum of the set { b-a | 0 <= a < b <= n and sum(a,b) = k }, with the maximum of the empty set defined to be 0. Equivalently, r is the greatest length of a non-empty contiguous subarray of nums whose elements sum to k, or 0 if no such subarray exists.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000; and -1000000000 <= k <= 1000000000.
